chapters.title: Circuit Breaker Pattern in Microservices Architecture

notes.text: The diagram shows a Microservices Architecture using Spring boot and Spring Cloud with a React App calling an API Gateway, which routes to three services: Employee Service, Department Service, and Organization Service backed by Databases, plus infrastructure components Config Server, Service Registry, Spring Cloud Sleuth, ZIPKIN, and GitHub.

notes.text: When the Department Service is down and Employee Service won't get a response, the Employee Service will send an internal server error to the API Gateway, which then sends that error back to the client.

notes.text: The Circuit Breaker pattern helps avoid continuous calls to a down service: it returns a default response to the client and sends a fallback response, preventing the API Gateway from repeatedly calling the failed Department Service.

chapters.summary: This section explains how the Circuit Breaker pattern prevents cascading failures when a dependent service is down, using Employee and Department services as an example, and introduces a simple Spring Boot and Spring Cloud microservices project structure.

tldr: This lecture outlines building an employee management project as microservices architecture using Spring Boot and Spring Cloud. The viewer learns the plan for three core services with separate MySQL databases, inter-service communication, service registry with Eureka, Config Server, API Gateway, distributed tracing with Sleuth and Zipkin, and circuit breaker plus React frontend.
